content:
Ken: Observed an odd class of SSE resumes where clients receive a stale partial payload after a resume. Seems correlated with sticky-routing flags toggling on scale events.
Maya: interesting. Any console anomalies?
Ken: per-route "live_streams" briefly reports +1 then -1, and customers see an extra short chunk that looks like a replay of an earlier partial message. Example trace below.
Ollie: paste logs?
Ken: ```
[2026-03-30T04:12:01Z] node=rt-a sticky=true accept_resume resume_ns=ns-101 session=s-7 token=abc
[2026-03-30T04:12:01Z] node=rt-a emit chunk=11 session=s-7
[2026-03-30T04:12:01Z] scaler: toggle sticky=false for node=rt-a -> migrate session=s-7
[2026-03-30T04:12:01Z] router: route resume token=abc -> rt-b (resume_ns=ns-101)
[2026-03-30T04:12:01Z] node=rt-b accept_resume resume_ns=ns-101 session=s-7
[2026-03-30T04:12:01Z] node=rt-b emit chunk=12 session=s-7
[2026-03-30T04:12:01Z] client_recv chunk=12
[2026-03-30T04:12:02Z] client_recv chunk=11
```
Ken: notice node rt-a emitted chunk 11 before the migration completed; client sees 12 then 11. resume_ns matches and both nodes accepted same namespace concurrently.
Maya: we explicitly namespace resume tokens to avoid cross-tenant and cross-deployment conflicts, but we didn't account for sticky toggles that allow old nodes to keep accepting a namespace during TTL. That allows double-accept for short windows.
Ollie: was a sticky-ttl reduction just deployed? There was a scaling tweak last night to avoid hot nodes.
Maya: yes, config runtime/routing/2026-03-29/sticky-ttl was reduced from 500ms -> 150ms to make room for aggressive scaling. Might be too aggressive when combined with non-exclusive resume acceptance.
ConsoleTeam: console noticed a small rise in "inflight_counts" noise and showed two support tickets complaining about out-of-order messages. We should annotate route pages when resume_ns_accept_overlap > 0.
billing-bot: /note: duplicated arrivals can cause token double-counting. We recommend short-window dedupe on billing if infra cannot guarantee single-writer semantics.
Ken: Proposed short-term actions: 1) emit metric resume.namespace_overlap when two distinct nodes accept the same resume_ns within 1s; 2) revert sticky-ttl to 500ms for canary groups; 3) console: add an orange micro-badge "handoff in-progress" when metric spike occurs; 4) add a proxy debug flag to log resume acceptor id for tracing.
Ollie: alternative: make resume acceptance strictly single-writer by using a fast atomic lease mutation in the control-plane, but that requires extra RPCs and could slow tail. We need to weigh latency vs correctness.
Maya: I can push a quick hotfix toggle: for multiplexed sessions (header X-MPX=true) revert sticky-ttl to 500ms while we evaluate. That limits blast radius.
Ken: small debug patch for proxy:```
--- a/proxy/resume.go
+++ b/proxy/resume.go
@@ -210,6 +210,9 @@ func acceptResume(ns string, nodeID string) bool {
  if controlPlane.MarkAccepted(ns, nodeID) {
+    if detectOverlap(ns) {
+      metrics.Inc("resume.namespace_overlap")
+    }
    return true
  }
  return false
}
```
DeployBot: rollout start: runtime/routing/2026-03-30/sticky-ttl-rollup -> canary (id: d-10099).
DeployBot: canary update: 4 instances updated, health checks ok.
Ken: canary telemetry: resume.namespace_overlap on canary hosts dropped from 0.42% -> 0.01% after TTL revert for mp-x sessions. Good.
ConsoleTeam: will add the micro-badge and an explanatory tooltip: "Counts may spike briefly during session handoffs; we're rolling mitigations." Low-risk UI change.
billing-bot: billing watching. If duplicates persist we'll enable idempotent dedupe by (resume_ns, chunk_id) for 10s.
Ollie: next steps: 1) tradeoff doc on strict atomic lease for resume acceptance (Ollie/Maya), 2) longer test run with mpx traffic, 3) consider a resume_ns suffixing strategy to ensure old acceptors cannot accept after migration.
Ken: uploading a small reproducible client and the trace to the infra repro repo. Thanks all.
Maya: agreed. We'll keep canary for 6 hours and then decide.
DeployBot: canary monitoring started."
